issues.legal_issue: A tenant may challenge the dismissal of an interlocutory application for statutory protection in an appeal from the decree in the eviction suit without filing a separate appeal against the dismissal order.
material_facts: The landlords brought an eviction suit, and the tenants filed an application under the tenant-protection legislation in that suit.
The trial court dismissed the application and decreed eviction.
The tenants appealed the decree and challenged the dismissal of their application in the appellate proceedings.
The High Court treated the application as no longer pending because the tenants had not filed a separate appeal against its dismissal.
issues.conclusion: The tenants could challenge the interlocutory order in their appeal against the decree without bringing a separate appeal, and their application was to be treated as pending during the appeal and second appeal. The legal effect of the application remained for the High Court to consider.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act permits a tenant facing an eviction suit to apply to the court for relief. Under Section 105 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a party appealing a decree may challenge the correctness of an interlocutory order made in the suit. That principle applies to an order on a Section 9 application even though Section 9A provides for appeals from specified orders. No earlier case is relied upon for this holding.

rule.if: eviction_suit and tenant_filed_protection_application and application_order_was_interlocutory and tenant_appealed_decree

predicates.eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.tenant_filed_protection_application: The tenant applied for statutory protection in the eviction suit.
predicates.application_order_was_interlocutory: The court disposed of the tenant’s application as an interlocutory matter in the suit.
predicates.tenant_appealed_decree: The tenant appealed the decree made in the eviction suit.
predicates.interlocutory_order_challengeable_in_dec: The tenant may challenge the interlocutory order in the appeal against the decree without filing a separate appeal against that order.

issues.definition: When a tenant applies for protection in an eviction suit and appeals the decree, the tenant may challenge the interlocutory order on that application in the decree appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute over statutory protection must be remitted for clarification when the record leaves material aspects of the territorial extension and rescission of that protection unclear.
material_facts: The trial court and the appellate court reached different conclusions about the effect of successive extensions of the tenant-protection legislation to the town where the land was situated.
The record left unclear why the legislation had been extended to the town more than once, what effect a later rescission had, and why it was extended there again by a later amendment.
Those matters were material to deciding whether the tenants could claim the legislation’s protection.
issues.conclusion: The matter was remitted to the High Court to decide in accordance with law after clarifying the material aspects. The High Court could receive additional material or call for a finding from the lower courts.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the unresolved history and effect of the territorial extensions as material to the decision and directed further consideration by the High Court. It identified no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this remand direction.

predicates.appeal_in_eviction_dispute: A party appealed in a dispute over eviction and a tenant’s claim to statutory protection.
predicates.territorial_extension_history_unclear: The record did not make clear the sequence or effect of successive territorial extensions and a rescission of the protection legislation.
predicates.uncertainty_material_to_protection_entit: The unclear extension history could affect whether the tenant was entitled to statutory protection.
predicates.matter_remitted_for_clarification: The matter is sent back to the reviewing court for clarification and further decision, with additional material or findings available if needed.

issues.definition: When an appeal in an eviction dispute turns on an unclear territorial-extension history that may affect protection entitlement, the matter is remitted for clarification.
